extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kae and Christopher Kanan
extraction.citeAs: Kushal Kae and Christopher Kanan. Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4 [cs.CV] 15 Jun 2017
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper reviews multiple VQA datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES) collected via crowdsourcing, NLP algorithms deriving QA pairs from image captions, and synthetic scene generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from NYU-DepthV2, Microsoft COCO, YFCC100M, and synthetic cartoon imagery.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (questions and answers) were created by human annotators prompted to ask questions (e.g., 'Stump a smart robot', region-specific questions) and provide answers, or generated automatically using NLP algorithms on existing image captions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes inter-human agreement (e.g., 83.3% on COCO-VQA), disagreement on subjective/opinion-seeking questions, and the use of consensus-based evaluation metrics (AccuracyVQA, WUPS) to handle multiple correct or ambiguous answers.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 independent annotators per question (COCO-VQA), 3 questions per image (COCO-VQA), and an average of 5 human annotated ground truth answers per question (DAQUAR-consensus).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithms (used to derive QA pairs from captions in COCO-QA)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA can be used as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals to get information about images, and to improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Datasets contain severe language biases where questions can often be answered without the image (e.g., 'yes' is the answer to 59% of yes/no questions in COCO-VQA). Annotators tend to ask similar questions about holistic content, creating unbalanced answer distributions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include grammatical errors in auto-generated questions, subjective questions lacking a single objective answer, poor inter-human agreement on 'Why' questions, and evaluation metrics that can be 'gamed' by exploiting dataset biases rather than performing visual reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and validation of Visual Question Answering (VQA) algorithms, and serving as a Visual Turing Test for image understanding.
